title: Standby orchestration capacity worksheet — multi-region spare planning
content:
Purpose:
- Short worksheet to align on how much standby (spare) GPU capacity we need per region for cross-region failover and DR. Focused on operational allocation, warm-pool rotation, and churn assumptions for Q2/Q3 2026.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We should move from an ad-hoc reserve to a small, orchestrated standby fabric: a combination of local (in-region) hot spares for immediate absorption (3–5% of active fleet), cross-region cold-to-warm failover that can take over sustained surge (additional 6–10% buffer by paired region), and a rotating warm-pool (5% of fleet globally) to reduce cold-start time for new replicas. This worksheet breaks down numbers by region, proposes failover pairings, estimates cost delta (~4–7% capacity overhead), and lists next actions to automate orchestration and telemetry needed for safe rollouts.

Assumptions used in calculations:
- Average production GPU utilization baseline: 72% across fleets (observed Jan–Feb 2026).
- Peak surge multiplier for incidents: 1.45x average sustained for up to 6 hours.
- Target SLA absorb window: 30s median added latency, 99.9% request acceptance by using hot spares + pre-warmed lanes.
- Warm-up time for a cold GPU to accept serving traffic: 12–18 minutes; warm-pool reduced to <45s.
- Recovery/DR restore target: 4 hours to ramp to full capacity in region using cross-region replication and orchestration.
- GPU types in fleet: H100 (large), A100 (general), L4 (edge). Allocation mixes below.

Region inventory snapshot (Feb 2026):
- us-west1: total GPUs 2,400 (H100: 1200, A100: 900, L4: 300); in-use average 1,728 (72%); free/unallocated 672
- us-east4: total GPUs 1,800 (H100: 900, A100: 700, L4: 200); in-use avg 1,296; free 504
- eu-west1: total GPUs 1,200 (H100: 600, A100: 450, L4:150); in-use avg 864; free 336
- ap-southeast1: total GPUs 800 (H100: 300, A100: 350, L4:150); in-use avg 576; free 224

Reserve policy proposals (per-region):
- Local hot spare target: 4% of total region fleet (for immediate absorption of short failures). Rationale: covers instantaneous node failures and small colo/network blips.
- Cross-region backstop: ability to absorb an additional 8% of origin region's peak by routing to paired region (pairedband). This is implemented as pre-warmed fallback routes with QoS throttles and lower-priority queue.
- Global rotating warm-pool: 5% of global fleet kept in a warmed state and cycled weekly to avoid drift and reduce restoration time.

Numeric reserves (rounded):
- us-west1: hot spares = 96 GPUs (4%); cross-region backstop requirement to be provided by paired eu-west1 + us-east4: 192 GPUs (8% of us-west1).
- us-east4: hot spares = 72 GPUs; cross-region backstop => us-west1 + eu-west1: 144 GPUs.
- eu-west1: hot spares = 48 GPUs; cross-region backstop => us-west1 + ap-southeast1: 96 GPUs.
- ap-southeast1: hot spares = 32 GPUs; cross-region backstop => eu-west1 + us-east4: 64 GPUs.
- Global warm-pool target: ~300 GPUs (5% of total fleet of 6,200 = 310, round to 300 for operational simplicity).

Failover pairing & routing notes:
- Primary pairings (preferred low-latency absorb): us-west1 <-> us-east4 (east/west), eu-west1 <-> us-west1 (transatlantic absorb with traffic shaping), ap-southeast1 -> eu-west1 (asymmetric lane; only for sustained DR).
- Routing policy: immediate short-failure -> local hot spare. If local utilization crosses 90% and local hot spares exhausted -> automatic reroute to primary pairing with conservative token throttling. For >4h incidents, escalate to cross-region capacity autoscale with pre-approved burst budgets.

Operational playbook snippets:
- Incident stage A (node blip, <15m): shift requests to in-region hot spares, do not route cross-region. Notify infra team, mark affected host as quarantined.
- Stage B (sustained outage, 15–180m): activate primary pairing lanes up to backstop capacity; enable A/B traffic splitting to measure QoE delta.
- Stage C (region-wide DR, >180m): enable global warm-pool contributions and spin reserve replicas in secondary region (aim to meet 70% of demand within 60m, 100% within 4h).

Simulation scenarios (quick):
- Single AZ failure in us-west1 (3 racks, 160 GPUs offline): local hot spares cover 96 -> remaining deficit 64 GPUs -> absorbed by us-east4 pairing, expected QoE degradation: latency +60–120ms for affected requests; cost delta +0.9% for 6 hours.
- Burst surge (1.4x baseline for 4 hours in eu-west1): eu local hot spares exhausted -> cross-region failover adds 96 GPUs from us-west1/ ap-southeast1 mix; global warm-pool contributes 30 GPUs to reduce cold starts; estimated cost delta +1.8% for window.
- Full region outage (ap-southeast1, 8 hours): durable failover uses eu-west1 as primary backstop plus global warm-pool; restoration requires spinning 120 GPUs from committed spare images with automated KMS rekeying; expected RTO ~3.5 hours with current automation (target 4h).

Cost & headcount impact (high level):
- Estimated capacity overhead: 4–7% of current fleet = ~250–430 GPUs reserved or warmed on average (mix H100/A100/L4).
- Approx monthly cost delta (cloud-equivalent amortized): $190k–$330k (depends on GPU mix and preemption policies).
- Operational work: small automation sprint (3 sprints) to wire up orchestration (+1 SRE + 1 infra eng part time for 6 weeks).

Telemetry and gating (what we need to measure):
- Real-time spare utilization % (per-region, per-GPU-class) with 1m and 5m windows.
- Failover acceptance rate and tail latencies (p95/p99) for routed requests.
- Warm-pool health: time-since-last-rotation, average warm-up time, cache-warm miss rates.
- Cost burn delta vs planned budget; automated alert when reserve usage > 50% of target for >30m.

Action items (owner & timeline):
- (Priya) Draft DR allocation automation RFC with pairing rules — due 2026-03-12.
- (Miguel) Implement metric dashboards for spare utilization and failover latency — due 2026-03-19.
- (Hannah) Prototype warm-pool rotation lambda (image bake + pre-warm hooks) in staging — due 2026-03-26.
- (Omar) Add JIRA runbooks for Stage A/B/C and link to incident commander playbook — due 2026-03-15.

Open questions / risks:
- Can we legally cross-border shift certain customer workloads (data residency)? Need product/legal gating per-customer and per-model.
- Is 5% global warm-pool the right balance for L4-heavy workloads (edge)? Might need separate warm-pool targets by GPU class.
- Network egress and inter-region bandwidth costs under heavy failover could exceed forecasts—need billing simulation.
- Warm-pool image drift: nightly rotation vs weekly rotation tradeoffs (nightly increases churn/cost).

Appendix: quick math notes (rounded):
- Total fleet = 2,400 + 1,800 + 1,200 + 800 = 6,200 GPUs.
- 4% local hot spares (weighted) = 248 GPUs (~250).
- 8% cross-region buffer for single-region worst-case = 496 GPUs (~500) distributed across pairings.
- Global warm-pool 5% = 310 GPUs (round operationally to 300).

If we accept the above policy, first deliverables are the RFC + metrics + pilot in us-west1 (small subset: 120 GPUs reserved as hot spares + 30 GPUs in warm-pool) to validate assumptions before broad rollout.

Notes/footnotes: include references to linked artifacts for full runbooks and cost models. End of worksheet.
